claims.text: ASME V&V 10 and NAFEMS simulation-credibility guidance treat verification and validation as distinct activities used to assess and enhance computational-model credibility.

ETSU's CADD/CAM/CNC standard teaches designing from desired product edges before deriving downstream toolpath geometry; this study adopts the transferable principle that analysis geometry is downstream of the frozen engineering geometry.
The fixture geometry, 100 N load, aluminum elastic properties, support idealization, and convergence thresholds are independently created screening inputs rather than employer or production data.

Average load-hole transverse displacement changes from -1.480476 mm to -1.481445 mm between the two finest meshes, a 0.065% relative change, satisfying the predeclared 2% global-displacement mesh criterion.
claims.method: Three progressively finer Gmsh second-order tetrahedral meshes solved with CalculiX 2.23; compare average load-hole UZ.

claims.text: The geometry-derived variable-section analytical projection predicts -1.590861 mm at the load point versus -1.481445 mm for the finest solid model, a 7.39% relative deviation under the declared nominal load path.
claims.method: Numerical Simpson integration of Euler-Bernoulli compliance using net section width derived from the same edge/hole geometry, compared with finest C3D10 solid model.

claims.text: Maximum integration-point von Mises stress rises across the mesh ladder (55.60 -> 61.30 -> 62.80 MPa), so this run does not establish a converged local peak-stress quantity.
claims.method: Direct comparison of maximum CalculiX integration-point von Mises stress across the declared mesh ladder.

claims.text: Every numerical level closes applied-vs-support z-force equilibrium; the maximum absolute balance residual is 3.370e-5 N for the 100 N load.
claims.method: Sum CalculiX mounting-hole reaction-force output and compare with the exact distributed applied nodal load at each mesh level.

claims.text: Julia 1.13.0 independently reproduces the geometry-derived analytical response at -1.590860648 mm, identifies the exact nominal stress maximum at the support plane, and reparses every raw CalculiX deck/result set to reproduce displacement, reaction, force-balance, and integration-point stress evidence.
claims.method: Independent Julia implementation using adaptive integration plus direct parsing of the generated CalculiX input/result files.

claims.text: NIST measured selected AMB2022-01 bridge ridges by tactile CMM before and after partial EDM release, using nearby build-plate regions in the reference strategy; published deflection is the cut-state ridge height minus the initial-state ridge height.
For NIST specimen AMB2022-718-AMMT-B7-P2, the six published release deflections range from -0.0025 mm to 1.8088 mm, with the maximum magnitude at ridge 6.
claims.method: Recompute every published ridge deflection as cut height minus initial height, then summarize the six named measurements.

claims.text: 5 of 6 published ridge-deflection magnitudes exceed the reported 0.0043 mm expanded uncertainty (k=2); ridge 1 does not exceed that simple uncertainty screen.
claims.method: Compare each absolute published deflection with its reported expanded uncertainty without converting the comparison into a process-capability claim.

claims.text: The AMB2022-01 six-ridge physical case does not establish Cp/Cpk or production acceptance because it is a benchmark artifact without a product tolerance specification or production distribution.
claims.method: Check whether the evidence contains both production-distribution data and engineering specification limits required for a process-capability interpretation; it does not.

claims.text: NIST AMB2022-01 provides in-situ thermography-derived location-specific time-above-melting (TAM) and solid-cooling-rate (SCR) quantities; the benchmark documentation identifies Part 1 as the thermography part.

The current AMB2022-01 evidence is not eligible for a direct thermal-to-deflection predictor: the in-process thermography identity is B7-P1 while the published deflection CTQ is B7-P2, and no signal-to-ridge spatial registration is admitted.
claims.method: Parse build/part identities, require same physical specimen plus registered signal-to-CTQ geometry, and fail closed when either pairing requirement is absent.

claims.text: On 23 evidence-clean same-track DED observations at 1000 W, adding active-frame IR features reduces leave-one-powder-flow-level-out bead-width RMSE from 0.4683 mm to 0.4279 mm (8.6% reduction) and raises pooled held-out R-squared from 0.250 to 0.374.
claims.method: Standardized ridge regression with fixed lambda=10; group-held-out comparison of recipe-only versus recipe plus two laser-active IR features.

claims.text: Leave-one-speed-level-out testing remains below zero held-out R-squared (-0.201), so the current model does not support extrapolation to unseen travel-speed levels.
claims.method: Hold out each commanded travel-speed level as an unseen group and evaluate the same fixed model family.

claims.text: NIST process-control guidance distinguishes statistically derived control limits from engineering specification limits and treats process stability as a prerequisite for capability interpretation; current AIAG/VDA SPC guidance likewise frames SPC as a connected control loop rather than an isolated chart.

The real DED treatment stops after within-window process-to-CTQ prediction: MSA is not assessable, capability is not assessable, and SPC is not active because the source lacks a crossed/equivalent measurement study, production population with engineering specifications, and qualified production time series.
claims.method: Evaluate required downstream quality evidence as explicit typed gates and fail closed when prerequisites are missing.

claims.text: The synthetic downstream demonstration qualifies the declared measurement-system, stability, and capability gates, then detects its first special-cause signal at 10.26 mm while that observation remains inside the synthetic 9.4–10.6 mm specification; the OCAP lifecycle ends at requalificationRequired rather than automatic restart.
claims.method: Crossed ANOVA Gage R&R; I-MR baseline; gated Cp/Cpk and Pp/Ppk; fixed-limit monitoring; XState containment/requalification lifecycle.

claims.text: The selected interoperability boundaries match current primary specifications: STEP Part 21/AP242 for product exchange, QIF for quality/metrology information, OPC UA DataValue and namespace-qualified NodeIds for industrial data, MTConnect Agent sequence semantics for machine streams, Sparkplug B birth/session state over MQTT, and Nastran DAT/BDF/F06 family boundaries for CAE exchange.

The adapter suite normalizes AP242 product/revision identity, QIF characteristic measurements, OPC UA process values, MTConnect and Sparkplug process streams, MES unit/run/recipe genealogy, and CalculiX/Nastran structural outputs into vendor-neutral internal contracts while explicitly keeping live vendor certification false.
claims.method: Run deterministic recorded/open-format fixtures through protocol-specific parsers and failure cases, then inspect one canonical assessment object and receipt.

claims.text: Lead the portfolio with the reusable predictive-quality and process-control workflow plus its interoperability layer: real DED evidence through process-to-CTQ prediction, explicit downstream quality gates, and vendor-neutral adapters for product definition, CAE, process signals, genealogy, and metrology. Keep vendor certification and synthetic capability boundaries explicit.

hardConstraints.statement: Only public or independently created synthetic inputs may enter this study.
hardConstraints.verification: NOTICE.txt, source register, synthetic config, and repository review.

hardConstraints.statement: No solver result or analytical calculation may be represented as certified structural adequacy, life-safety approval, or production release.
hardConstraints.verification: Claim review and case-study limitations; physical validity requires separate correlation evidence.

hardConstraints.statement: Analytical and numerical projections must bind to the same frozen geometry/material/load revision.
hardConstraints.verification: Shared analysis/config.json and geometry digest in structural-analysis.json and structural-analysis-run.json.

hardConstraints.statement: Every idealization or omitted physical mechanism must be explicit; no reduced model may silently replace the geometry or assembly behavior.
hardConstraints.verification: analysis/ARCHITECTURE.md, modelForm block, decision 0001, and verification plan.

hardConstraints.statement: No physical-validity claim is admitted before measured test data or a trusted public benchmark is compared to the bound model revision with uncertainty recorded.
Capability and active SPC may not be represented as assessable before the measurement system and process baseline satisfy their declared qualification gates.
hardConstraints.verification: analysis/src/quality-system.ts, analysis/src/run-quality-system.ts, data/quality-control-workflow.json, and quality-system tests.

hardConstraints.statement: A future load test must use a bounded fixture and load application that does not require a person to hold or restrain the specimen during loading.
hardConstraints.verification: Future measurement-system and test-fixture plan before physical execution.

hypotheses.statement: The declared quadratic-solid model reaches a mesh-stable global load-hole displacement under the frozen rigid-hole support/load idealization.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject if progressive mesh refinement changes average load-hole transverse displacement by more than the predeclared 2% criterion.

hypotheses.statement: A geometry-derived variable-section Euler-Bernoulli projection predicts global load-hole displacement within the predeclared 20% diagnostic band of the finest solid model under the same nominal load path.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject if analytical-to-finest-FEA displacement deviation exceeds 20% for the frozen model revision.

hypotheses.statement: The present mesh sequence is sufficient to make a stable local peak-stress claim near holes/support features.
hypotheses.falsification: Support only after a stress-focused refinement/error study demonstrates stability at the declared region and quantity.

hypotheses.statement: The as-built bolted/base fixture will be more compliant than the current rigid-hole numerical idealization, making interface/base compliance a likely source of future prediction-to-test discrepancy.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject if a controlled physical test with measured setup geometry shows equal or lower displacement than the bound rigid-hole prediction within measurement uncertainty.

hypotheses.statement: At least five of the six published AMB2022-01 ridge release-deflection magnitudes exceed their reported expanded uncertainty for specimen AMB2022-718-AMMT-B7-P2.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject if deterministic recomputation from the published initial/cut heights and uncertainty table yields fewer than five ridge magnitudes above the reported expanded uncertainty.

hypotheses.statement: The currently identified AMB2022-01 in-process thermal features can be treated as paired predictors of the published ridge-deflection CTQ.
hypotheses.falsification: Support only when thermal signals and final CTQ are from the same physical part and the signal locations are registered to the measured CTQ features.

hypotheses.statement: Same-track in-process IR features improve held-out bead-width prediction relative to recipe-only inputs inside the curated DED process window.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject if leave-one-powder-flow-level-out RMSE is not lower after adding the admitted active-frame IR features.

hypotheses.statement: The current DED model generalizes to an entirely unseen travel-speed level.
hypotheses.falsification: Support only if grouped holdout on travel-speed levels produces positive held-out R-squared with stable error.

hypotheses.statement: A reusable evidence-first workflow can block unsupported real-data capability claims while executing MSA, stability, capability, SPC, containment, and requalification on a clearly separated synthetic production stream.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject if the real DED path reaches capability/SPC without the missing evidence, or if the synthetic gate chain bypasses MSA/stability or fails to require requalification after the special-cause event.

hypotheses.statement: External product, process, metrology, genealogy, and solver formats can be normalized into canonical engineering identities without coupling the analytical core to one vendor.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject if any adapter loses revision/genealogy/session identity, accepts invalid protocol state, or requires vendor-specific types in the analytical core.

payload.question: How should geometry and process parameters change together to improve CNC, additive, assembly, inspection, maintenance, and end-of-life outcomes?
